• DLG • bYAENG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cora Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE ATTY. ENERIO M. SABULAO Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Eastern Samar Dear SP Member Sabulao: DILG Legal Opinion No. 81 s. 2011 NOV 2 3 2011 This has reference to your letter dated 23 September 2011 requesting Secretary Jesse M. Robredo to resolve the alleged conflicting opinions of DILG- Region VIII and this Service. It may be recalled that thru a letter dated 23 May 201 1, you sought the opinion of DILG-Region VIII on the following issues, which we quoted in toto: How many votes are required to pass an Annual or Supplemental Budget? 2. What is legal effect of the declaration by the chair that the Supplemental Budget passed and approved despite the hard fact that out of all the 74 members present only 7 members voted in favor thereof? 3. Assuming that the position of the undersigned is correct, what actions or steps must be undertaken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Secretary on the Appropriation Ordinance/Supplemental Budget to prevent immediate disbursement of funds?" Thereafter, DILG-Region VIII Director Francisco C. Jose rendered a legal opinion dated 26 May 201 1 addressed to you where he cited DILG Opinion No. 13, series of 2010. In gist, DILG-Region VIII opined that in a regular session attended by all 14 members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the vote of eight (8) members is required to pass an Annual or Supplemental Budget. With seven (7) members voting for the approval thereof and six (6) members against it, our DILG-Region VIII concluded that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Eastern Samar was not able to muster the required vote for the passage of the Supplemental Budget so that the budget should be deemed invalid, contrary to the declaration of the Presiding Officer that the same was duly passed and approved. DILG-Region VIII finally advised the Sangguniang Panlalawigan not to indorse the Appropriation Ordinance/Supplemental Budget to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) for review and thus be treated to comply with the vote requirement. On 17 June 201 1, this Service received the letter dated 14 June 201 1 of Vice- Governor Gonzales to the undersigned requesting a legal opinion on the same issues posed to DILG-Region VIII. In the sarne letter, Vice—Governor Gonzales already informed us about the opinion rendered by DILG-Region VIII and made a representation that "xxx the budget has been considered passed and approved".

Thus, thru a letter dated 28 June 201 1, the undersigned wrote Vice-Governor Gonzales, pertinent portion of which reads: "Ergo, since the aforesaid Supplemental Budget is already an approved ordinance, the same enjoys the presumption of validity, hence, precludes this Department from rendering an opinion thereon. Hence, your letter requesting Secretary Robredo to resolve the alleged conflicting opinions of DILG-Region VIII and this Service. In this regard, please be informed that there is no conflict between the two (2) opinions. In fact, the opinion rendered by this Service complements the opinion rendered by DILG-Region VIII. As discussed above, in the opinion rendered by this Service, we accorded the Ordinance approving the Supplemental Budget the presumption of validity. Such presumption was due to the representation made by Vice-Governor Gonzales in his letter dated 14 June 201 that said budget has been considered passed and approved with seven (7) votes voting in favor of its passage and six (6) against it. Let it be noted that the presumption on the regularity of the enactment of an officially promulgated statute or ordinance has the primary purpose of securing certainty where doubt would be intolerable. Such presumption may not be impeached by parol evidence or oral testimony either of individual officers and members, or of strangers who may be interested in nullifying legislative action. This rule supplements the presumption in favor of the regularity of official conduct, absent a clear showing to the contrary (Figuerres vs. CA, 305 SCRA 206 [7 9991). There being a declaration made by Vice-Governor Gonzales, as Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, after the vote among the members of said Augwst Body that the Ordinance approving the Supplemental Budget has been passed and approved by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, we are of the view, as we intimated in our 28 June 201 1 letter to Vice-Governor Gonzales, that the said Ordinance has been duly passed and approved as declared by Vice- Governor Gonzales. Applying the ruling of the Supreme Cowrt in the Figuerres case, such presumption may not be impeached by parol evidence or oral testimony either of individual officers and members, or of strangers who may be interested in nullifying legislative action. Along this line, it may be well to stress that Vice-Governor Gonzales is also a public official to which he enjoys in his favor the presumption of the regularity of official conduct. Hence, before Vice-Governor made his declaration, he is presumed to have taken into account the pertinent law, rules and regulations on the matter under consideration. Any question as to the validity of the Ordinance authorizing the Supplemental Budget (e.g. failure of the Sangguniang Pan/alawigan to muster the required vote for the passage of the Ordinance authorizing the Supplemental Budget) should already be threshed out before the proper forum by filing the appropriate pleading, the matter being adjudicatory in nature. The foregoing was the reason why in our letter dated 28 June 201 1 to Vice- Governor Gonzales, we stated therein that the Department, given the set of facts, was precluded from rendering an opinion thereon. In fact, this has already been set as a Department policy in DILG Memorandum Order No. 2070-02, dated 17 September 2010, entitled: "Supplement to Memorandum Order No. 2070-01 dated March 4 2010," wherein it was stated that the Department shall not act on queries

regarding those presumptively valid acts, e.g. enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances. What if despite the foregoing, an opinion was still rendered just like what happened in the case at hand when DILG-Region VIII previously rendered a legal opinion dated 26 May 201 1 addressed to you discussing point by point the issues you raised in your letter to our Regional Office dated 23 May 201 1, will there be inconsistency in the position of this Service as discussed above and our Regional Office? There is none. The subject Ordinance authorizing the Supplemental Budget and Vice- Governor Gonzales in making his previous declaration enjoy the presumption of validity and presumption of regularity, respectively. The legal opinion rendered by DILG-Region VIII dated 26 May 2011 should be considered as an academic discussion to guide you and all others who are in doubt as to the validity of the subject Ordinance authorizing the Supplemental Budget on what to do under the given circumstances. The discussion made by DILG-Region VIII as to the legal infirmity of the Ordinance authorizing the Supplemental Budget may be used as your basis in challenging its validity before the proper forum and should not be considered as a declaration of the invalidity of the subject Ordinance. Let it be noted that this Department has no authority to declare invalid any ordinance declared to have been passed and approved by the sanggunian concerned. Let it be noted further that the burden of showing that the Ordinance authorizing the Supplemental Budget suffers from legal infirmity falls on you and all other complainants. We hope this finally settles your concern. Very truly yours, Ls/17 Copy furnished: RD FRANCISCO C. JOSE DILG-Region VIII Kanhuraw Hill, Tacloban City VICE-GOVERNOR CHRISTOPHER SHEEN P. GONZALES Provincial Capitol, Eastern Samar
